annotations.title: Open a CI cost fix PR (draft)

description: Open a DRAFT pull request that applies one CI cost fix to one workflow file (ADR 0047), the fix a CI advice item offers as autofix (get_ci_overview / get_ci_costs advice[].autofix { kind, projectId, repo, workflowPath }). kind: add_concurrency (a concurrency group that cancels superseded pull request runs, never a push), skip_drafts (ready_for_review added to the pull_request types and every job skips drafts), weekly_cron (a schedule that fires more than weekly runs once a week), ignore_docs_paths (paths-ignore for docs-only changes, Markdown, docs/, license and issue templates, on pull_request and push; refused when a job looks like a required check, because a skipped workflow never reports and the PR could not merge). The repo must be connected to the project. Mushi reads the workflow from the default branch, edits only that file (comments kept), opens the PR as a draft with a conventional ci: title, and records the workflow's billed minutes per day for the 14 days before; nothing changes until a person reviews, readies and merges it. The job runs in the background: read it again with the job id (GET /v1/admin/ci/cost-fixes/{id}, or `mushi runner fix-status`); after the merge it shows the saving measured per day. Writing a workflow file needs the GitHub App's Workflows: Read and write permission or a token with the workflow scope. Confirm with the user first. Returns { job: { id, status (queued | running | pr_opened | no_change | refused | failed), summary, errorCode, error, prUrl, baseline, measured, saving } }, or an error (REPO_NOT_IN_PROJECT, PR_ALREADY_OPEN with the job, COST_FIX_IN_PROGRESS, RATE_LIMITED: 10 an hour per project). Write.

projectId.description: Project UUID — defaults to the server-configured project (`project_id` is accepted too.)
